chunks: When the hypocrites, and those who had doubts in their hearts, said: "Their faith has misled them." But whoever places his trust in God will find God mighty and wise.
ai.seo_question: What did the hypocrites say about the Muslims' faith after the Battle of Badr?
ai.summary: In the context of the Battle of Badr, this verse highlights the psychological shift of the Munafiqun, who initially viewed the Muslims' reliance on God as naivety but later saw it as the source of their victory. Shia scholarship emphasizes that 'those with disease in their hearts' refers to a spiritual malady of doubt that persists even amidst clear signs, contrasting with the steadfast Tawakkul of the believers. The affirmation of Allah's 'Aziz' (Mighty) and 'Hakim' (Wise) attributes serves to validate the divine strategy behind the seemingly fragile trust of the early Muslim community.
